description.narrative: The programme aims to enhance conditions for inclusive governance, peace and the promotion and protection of human rights and gender equality in Afghanistan. The programme will focus on 1) enhancing access to concrete recommendations and potential solutions, aimed to more effectively promote human rights, including gender equality, 2) increasing scholarships and academic discourse on human rights situation, incluidng in relation to gender equality, 3) sustaining and/or improving capacities of Afghan researchers to generate high quality research that contributes to montoring, promoting and protecting human rights in Afghanistan and 4) augmenting the capabilities of Afghan human rights defenders and civil society to actively engage with UN mechanisms, working for human rights, gender equality and inclusive governance in Afganistan. The intended target group for this programme is Afghan human rights scholars and Afghan human rights defenders. The programme is aslo facilitating and supporting synergies with the UN Special Rapporteur (UNSR) on the situation of Human Rights in Afghanistan, Richard Bennett, who is hosted by the Raoul Wallenberg Institute (RWI) as a guest professor. Research and expertise from a diverse group of Afghan scholars in this programme, along with outcomes from expert/practitioners roundtables on issues related to the UNSR mandate, contribute to UNSR Bennett's reports and recommendations presented to the Human Rights Council and the UN General Assembly. Additionally, this information informs his assistance and advice to civil society and other pertinent stakeholders.
